replay.fixtureRelocation: Only PdfReader file access is mapped to original SHA/size-verified artifact PDFs. Config/event absolute paths and all ownership comparisons remain byte-for-byte original. Entire validate_result and its helper function ASTs are compiled unchanged from the pinned source, without launch/build code.

findings.conclusion: All compared A/B/C runs retain native text, geometry and full-page raster parity, and capture a matching ready viewer image. No acceleration claim.

findings.scope: shared-fonts engine ABBA, n=2 per arm
findings.conclusion: A refreshes source-0 only (opens 2/1/1); source-1 misses geometry/raster parity and a matching viewer frame in 2/2. B refreshes both affected sources (2/2/1) and restores full parity in 2/2, with only two native font registrations and one backend reload per process.

findings.scope: different-fonts engine ABBA, n=2 per arm
findings.conclusion: A has one resource-attribution mismatch per process and fails source-1 geometry/raster parity; B has zero and restores both sources. The PDFs have different requested faces but share the explicit Helvetica control resource.

findings.scope: late-page and late-text app BCCB, n=2 per arm per scenario
findings.conclusion: B registers no missing fonts and leaves geometry/raster mismatched, despite equal extracted text. C handles the late native event, performs two registrations/one backend reload, reopens only source-0 once (2/1 opens), and restores native and viewer parity in all four C processes.

findings.scope: close-pending-font app BCCB, n=2 per arm
findings.conclusion: B starts an extra source open after closeRequested and gate release in 2/2; C does not in 2/2. Both still finish the in-flight registrations. Native close futures complete, and the unrelated viewer remains correct.

findings.scope: one separate B diagnostic each for initial-hebrew, late-page and close-pending-font
findings.conclusion: Initial-hebrew and late-page have zero framework/capture errors and matching native/viewer parity. Close-pending-font avoids the after-close open but records TWO framework errors (one distinct stack): Null check operator used on a null value, PdfViewerController._state -> documentRef -> associateFontManager callback after detach. Therefore that diagnostic is NOT an error-free lifecycle success or a recommendation to substitute the built-in manager. These single launches are not ABBA comparisons and do not establish all replacement/completed-skip lifecycle behavior.

The original Actions run fails at the C warmup because it counts a deliberate source replacement as an unwanted font-free-peer reopen. Strict post-download replay accepts that one existing warmup with owner, gate, close, target-page and RGBA checks; the replacement ABBA blocks were not executed in this run.

limitations: Linux x64 profile, synthetic unembedded-font fixtures; this is not a real-book or cross-platform performance result.
A/B and B/C each have only two fresh independent processes per arm in one ABBA block per scenario. Warmups/builtin/frames are not additional independent samples.
No B-arm pooling between engine/app blocks and no time pooling with another workflow run.
Native final text/geometry/raster parity is relative to a fresh-open reference with the same resolver policy, not an external rendering ground truth.

First-good is the completion time of the first captured matching ready RepaintBoundary image: an upper bound. Final capture, PNG work, quiet waits and sparse sampling prevent a product latency/speedup conclusion.
No mismatching ready sample does not prove that no fallback image was displayed between samples, and the captured layer tree is not OS scanout.
The initial Hebrew and Latin C/B median observed upper-bound ratios are retained even if higher; they are not silently classified as a speedup or a measured product regression.
Lifecycle/shared fixtures deliberately gate font registration; gated times are not natural performance estimates.
Actual recorded native font queries use charset 0 here; Hebrew text in the fixture does not prove a native charset-177 request or a change to Hebrew/ANSI policy.
Native registration events identify a face, whereas manager requests have five fields/context; absent registration is not equivalent to a manager unresolved/failed result.

The archived bundle/compiler/native receipts were verified by the live host; executable/AOT/library bytes are not duplicated in this raw artifact, so offline analysis checks receipt consistency rather than re-observing a live process.
The final replacement scenario has no complete comparison block in this run. Its extra warmups are not pooled with the separate follow-up.
